title: And that’s not even all of them! #broadway #xmen #theatre #westend #c...
transcript: So the theater community is buzzing about how many of the newly announced X men actors have recently been on Broadway. And yes, I'm very excited about it too. But I do think it's worth noting that the X men film series actually has a very long history of casting actors who are no strangers to the stage. Of course, the most prominent examples of this are Hugh Jackman as Wolverine, who actually got his start doing musical theater in Australia before he was Wolverine and has done a lot of Broadway shows since. And of course, real life besties Patrick Stewart and Ian Mckellen as Professor X and Magneto, respectively, who are of course, two of the most accomplished stage actors currently living and have performed together even many times. But of course we can't forget Broadway favorite Alan Cumming as Nightcrawler. Long time stage veteran Kelsey Grammer as Beast. Anna Paquin, who played Rogue, had several off Broadway credits before she played this role. James Mcavoy, who also played Professor X, has multiple stage credits, including most recently Jamie Lloyd's Cyrano de Bergerac. We have Brian Cox, one of the most memorable villains in the series. He's been on stage a lot, including most recently Long Day Journey Into night in London. Most recently on Broadway, he played LBJ in the Great Society. Then one of the least memorable villains: We also had Oscar Isaac. He also got his start on stage before he was famous, but most recently he Was in The Sign in Sidney Brustein’s window on Broadway. We have Liev Schreiber in the Wolverine movie, who was most recently in Doubt on Broadway. Ben Foster as Angel, who's done a lot of stage work, including playing Stanley Kowalski in streetcar. Of course, we can't forget recent Tony nominee Rose Byrne, who played Moira Mctaggert in the X men movies. We had Peter Dinklage as Trask, seen most recently on stage in Twelfth Night. Evan Jongkeit as Toad has tons of stage credits going way back. Same with Bruce Davison, who plays Senator Kelly in the first two films. He's been doing stage work for decades. And of course, we can't forget Broadway favorite Brian d’Arcy James in the extremely memorable role as the president of the United States in Dark Phoenix.
classificationReason: Commentary about X-Men film actors who have stage experience. Discusses many actors and productions in passing but reviews none; the subject is the casting pattern in the X-Men film franchise, not any specific stage production.
